$comment: Configuration template for the review-graph pack. `agency add review-graph` copies it to <project>/.agency/review-graph.json and fills in what it can detect. This file is owned by the PROJECT — a pack upgrade never overwrites it.

repo.$comment_slug: owner/repo. `agency init` fills it in from the git remote.

brief.$comment: Optional. A standing focus for every review of this project, e.g. "pay extra attention to Supabase policies". A one-off focus is `agency run review-graph --pr 12 --prompt "…"`. The brief prioritises, it never overrides the gate: a finding without evidence stays dropped no matter what the brief says.

graph.$comment_onStale: update = index incrementally (fast, the right thing for a PR) | build = rebuild from scratch (expensive, only when the graph is missing) | ignore

worktree.$comment_path: A throwaway worktree. Nothing is ever checked out into the user's working copy — their branch and their work in progress stay untouched. Placeholders: {repo} {n} {hire} {provider} {model}. Keep {hire} in the path — two specialists reviewing the same pull request in parallel need two directories, and without it the second one would delete the first one's work.

agent.$comment: The fallback for a run that has no hire behind it. Who normally does the work is the roster — `agency roster`, `agency hire review-graph --provider codex`. This block still decides the launch shape (binary, extra flags) and it applies to `provider` below and to nobody else.
agent.$comment_model: null = keep the provider default model. The choice is written into the run record so you can measure which model produces better findings.

review.$comment_dimensions: repo-rules is added once you fill in `rules` below. Without project rules 4 of 5 dimensions run — that is a legitimate outcome, not a failure.
review.$comment_rules: A pointer to the section with the project rules, e.g. 'CLAUDE.md#rules-that-will-bite-you'. The content of that section belongs to the project, not to the pack.
review.$comment_docMap: A section mapping touched paths to documentation, e.g. 'CLAUDE.md#where-the-truth-lives'. Without it the documentation is not looked up.
review.$comment_verifyCommand: What CI does, e.g. 'npm run verify'. It is used to drop findings CI would catch anyway — not to run anything.

sinks.$comment_runRecord: Always true. The run record is the truth, everything else is a derived sink — if a sink fails, the finding is not lost.
sinks.$comment_githubProject: The GitHub Project number for the one-way export, or null. There is no sync back.
